description: Defines the structural model of bifurcation events, attractor basins, and trajectory splitting. A bifurcation event occurs when a trajectory reaches a configuration from which two or more successor configurations are possible under the governing transformation, or when a discontinuous configuration gap is detected by PD-Τ. This map covers bifurcation event classification, attractor identification, basin computation, and the formal conditions for trajectory splitting. Binds to INV-PD-001 (Trajectory Continuity — bifurcations are the exception class) and INV-PD-002 (Attractor Stability — attractors are the convergence targets post-bifurcation).

bifurcation_definition.formal: bifurcation_event(B) = ⟨S_b, t_b, {S'_1, S'_2, ..., S'_k}, τ_trigger, basin_assignments⟩

components.S_b: The bifurcation configuration — the structural configuration at which the bifurcation occurs
components.t_b: The bifurcation time-point — the trajectory index at which S_b is reached
components.S'_1..k: The set of k ≥ 2 successor configurations reachable from S_b under declared transformations
components.τ_trigger: The transformation condition that triggers the bifurcation — the parameter or constraint that crosses a threshold at t_b
components.basin_assignments: The attractor basin assignment for each successor S'_i — which attractor each continuation trajectory is expected to converge toward

bifurcation_definition.structural_note: A bifurcation event is not a failure — it is a structural branch point. Book 9 does not penalize bifurcations; it requires they be formally logged and that each continuation trajectory be independently traced by PD-Τ.
bifurcation_definition.gap_reclassification: Configuration gaps detected by PD-Τ (adjacent configurations not bridged by any declared transformation) are reclassified as unclassified bifurcation events B_unclassified and submitted to PD-Β for trigger identification. If no trigger can be identified, the gap is logged as a trajectory integrity failure under INV-PD-001.

bifurcation_types.label: Parameter Bifurcation
bifurcation_types.description: A bifurcation triggered by a transformation parameter crossing a critical threshold. Below the threshold, the trajectory converges to attractor A_1; above it, the trajectory converges to attractor A_2 (or diverges). The bifurcation point is the parameter value at which A_1 loses stability.
bifurcation_types.formal: parameter_bifurcation(τ, θ) ⟺ ∃θ_c: ∀θ < θ_c: τ^n(S) → A_1  ∧  ∀θ > θ_c: τ^n(S) → A_2
cross_book_instances: GRL authority decay: λ_R crossing a critical decay rate triggers regime collapse bifurcation — trajectory splits into recovery trajectory or collapse trajectory
OR opacity: ω crossing the revelation threshold δ(O) triggers a reveal/remain-opaque bifurcation
NoS abstraction: INV-NOS-004 abstraction consistency failure triggers upward-revision bifurcation

bifurcation_types.label: Constraint Bifurcation
bifurcation_types.description: A bifurcation triggered by the addition or removal of a constraint from the governing constraint set C. Constraint addition restricts the reachable successor set; constraint removal expands it. Either can produce multiple viable continuation trajectories.
bifurcation_types.formal: constraint_bifurcation(C, C') ⟺ reachable_successors(S, C) ≠ reachable_successors(S, C')
cross_book_instances: GRL constraint enforcement: addition of a new regime constraint C_new to C_R splits governed structure trajectories into compliant and non-compliant continuations
SARG defeat: defeat of a constraint node in C_A (INV-SARG-003) removes constraint coverage, expanding the continuation trajectory space
TEL assertion: adding an INV[ID] assertion to a TEL expression in mid-evaluation creates a constraint bifurcation — expressions satisfying the invariant continue; others halt

bifurcation_types.label: Dissolution Bifurcation
bifurcation_types.description: A bifurcation in which one or more continuation trajectories lead directly to the dissolution region. At least one continuation is dissolution-bound; if all continuations are dissolution-bound, the bifurcation is a terminal dissolution event. If some continuations survive, the surviving trajectories are traced by PD-Τ and the dissolved trajectories are logged.
bifurcation_types.pd_action: PD-Β classifies each continuation as surviving or dissolving. Dissolving continuations are handed to PD-Μ for mutation constraint evaluation — if the dissolved pattern has a mutation anchor in a surviving continuation, the dissolution is reclassified as a mutation event rather than a terminal event.
cross_book_instances: GRL collapse: α(R) reaching collapse threshold triggers a dissolution bifurcation — regime either reconstitutes or dissolves
SARG argument total defeat: defeat of all paths to root(A) produces a dissolution bifurcation for the argument structure
NoS identity loss: INV-NOS-003 violation (no invariant preservation) produces a dissolution bifurcation

bifurcation_types.label: Synthesis Bifurcation
bifurcation_types.description: A bifurcation unique to Book 9 as the synthesis terminal. When cross-book pattern streams from multiple upstream books arrive at PD-Τ simultaneously and produce conflicting trajectory steps, a synthesis bifurcation is triggered. The synthesis bifurcation resolves which upstream pattern stream takes precedence at the contested trajectory step.
bifurcation_types.formal: synthesis_bifurcation ⟺ ∃i, j ∈ upstream_books: trajectory_step(i, t_b) ≠ trajectory_step(j, t_b)
bifurcation_types.resolution_procedure: PD-Β applies the following precedence order for synthesis bifurcation resolution: (1) NoS meta-structural invariants override domain-specific invariants; (2) TEL formal encoding takes precedence over informal descriptions; (3) Higher-tier books (Capstone > Applied > Core Tool > Intermediate > Foundation) have precedence in case of remaining conflict.
bifurcation_types.pd_action: PD-Β records the synthesis bifurcation event with all conflicting upstream inputs and the resolution outcome. PD-Σ receives the full bifurcation log for synthesis reporting.

attractor_model.title: Structural Attractor Identification
attractor_model.formal: attractor(A, τ) ⟺ ∀S: dist(S, A) < ε → lim_{n→∞} τ^n(S) = A  [INV-PD-002]
attractor_model.distance_metric: dist(S, A) = 1 - (|invariant_set(S) ∩ invariant_set(A)| / |invariant_set(A)|)  — structural distance is the proportion of A's invariants that S fails to satisfy

attractor_types.label: Fixed-Point Attractor
attractor_types.description: A single configuration A such that τ(A) = A. All nearby trajectories converge to A and remain there. The simplest attractor class.
attractor_types.cross_book: GRL stable authority regime: α(R) converges to a stable value where compliance exactly compensates decay — a fixed-point attractor in authority state-space
attractor_types.basin_computation: Basin = all S with dist(S, A) < ε under the governing τ

attractor_types.label: Periodic Attractor
attractor_types.description: A cycle of configurations A_0, A_1, ..., A_{k-1}, A_0 such that τ(A_i) = A_{i+1 mod k}. Trajectories in the basin converge to the cycle but do not settle at a single configuration.
attractor_types.cross_book: SARG warrant-defeat cycles: argument configurations cycling between warrant-challenged and warrant-restored states without final resolution
attractor_types.basin_computation: Basin = all S from which trajectories eventually enter and remain in the k-cycle

attractor_types.label: Structural Attractor
attractor_types.description: A set of configurations A that share a common invariant subset — the attractor invariant core. Trajectories converge to A when they accumulate the attractor invariant core, without necessarily reaching a single fixed configuration.
attractor_types.formal: structural_attractor(A) ⟺ ∃I_core ⊆ ⋂{invariant_set(a) : a ∈ A}: every trajectory from the basin eventually satisfies I_core
attractor_types.cross_book: NoS structural realism attractor: all trajectory continuations that satisfy INV-NOS-001 and INV-NOS-002 converge to the OSR (Ontic Structural Realism) attractor
attractor_types.pd_note: Structural attractors are the primary attractor class in Book 9 — they subsume fixed-point and periodic attractors as special cases.

attractor_verification_procedure.action: Identify candidate attractor configuration A from the convergent trajectory classification by PD-Τ
Compute invariant_set(A) — the full set of invariants satisfied by A across all eight upstream book invariant registries
Select at least three nearby configurations S_1, S_2, S_3 with dist(S_i, A) < ε
Apply the governing transformation τ repeatedly to each S_i and verify convergence to A within a bounded step count
Compute the basin boundary: the set of configurations at which convergence to A is no longer guaranteed
Record: attractor_id, invariant_set(A), basin_boundary, convergence_step_count, attractor_type (AT-001/002/003)

basin_computation_model.description: Attractor basins partition the state-space into convergence regions. Basin computation is performed by PD-Β after attractor verification.
basin_computation_model.formal: basin(A, τ) = { S ∈ SS : lim_{n→∞} τ^n(S) = A }
basin_computation_model.basin_boundary: ∂basin(A) = { S : S ∈ basin(A) ∧ ∃ε > 0 ∀δ < ε ∃S': dist(S, S') < δ ∧ S' ∉ basin(A) }
basin_computation_model.multi_attractor_partition: When multiple attractors exist in SS, the basins partition SS (possibly with measure-zero boundaries): SS = basin(A_1) ∪ basin(A_2) ∪ ... ∪ basin(A_m) ∪ ∂basins ∪ dissolution_region
cross_book_basin_feeds: GRL: regime stability/collapse basin boundary determined by critical α threshold and λ_R decay rate
SARG: valid/invalid argument basin boundary determined by INV-SARG-001 through INV-SARG-004 satisfaction
NoS: OSR/ESR/dissolution basin boundary determined by INV-NOS-001 and INV-NOS-002 joint satisfaction
